title: August and the Undertow
premise: Rosalind Brightwater, a piano tuner who reads a house's past in its pipes and floorboards, has spent thirty years in the coastal town of August Hollow pretending to be no one in particular. When Emeric Voss, the last fluent speaker of a dying trade-tongue called Undertow, asks her to become his final student, she must confront why she fled the Voss household as a girl—and what she did, or failed to do, the night his daughter drowned. As Emeric's memory fails faster than her lessons can hold it, Rosalind returns to the flooded quarry house where the story went wrong and finally speaks the truth aloud in a language only two people alive can understand. The book ends with Emeric's death and Rosalind teaching the first word of Undertow to a child on the beach: belonging, she learns, is not inherited but chosen, one utterance at a time.
about_author: T. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former marine archivist who spent a decade cataloguing recordings of endangered languages before turning to fiction. They live within earshot of the Atlantic and claim to tune their own piano badly, on purpose.

chapters.title: The Radiator Speaks First
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Tuning a piano in a decaying seaside hotel, she hears in the radiators the story of a family that once owned half the town—the Vosses—and flinches from her own connection to them. Emeric Voss appears at her door with an offer: teach me nothing, learn everything. The beat is unease disguised as routine; her invisibility begins to crack.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Drowning Tongue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Rosalind and Emeric. Lessons unfold in Emeric's salt-stained kitchen as his memory slips—words surface that Rosalind secretly already knows, betraying a childhood in his house. Flashbacks reveal the drowned daughter, Maren, and Rosalind's silence afterward. The beat is intimacy shadowed by guilt; loyalty to her old secrecy wars with the truth pressing upward like water.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Keeps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, climax. With Emeric hospitalized and forgetting fast, Rosalind returns to the drained quarry house where Maren died and reconstructs the night through the building's groans and echoes—discovering she was not guilty of causing the death but of letting Emeric believe a merciful lie. She brings him the truth in Undertow; he answers with forgiveness shaped like a lesson. The beat is catharsis at cost.

chapters.title: One Word, Passed On
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, resolution. After Emeric's quiet death, Rosalind records what remains of the language, then abandons her tenant's transience and buys the small house she has rented for years. On the beach she teaches a neighbor's child the first word of Undertow—the word for stay. The beat is quiet transformation: memory kept not by hoarding but by handing over.
